index.html.title: Introduction | Smart UI Scaler plugin
index.html.keywords: Introduction Smart UI Scaler is a powerful replacement for Unity's built-in Canvas Scaler component. It offers advanced, flexible scaling features that make it easy to design responsive UI layouts for any screen size or device. Features 🖼️ Broad Canvas Support Fully compatible with both Overlay and Camera screen space canvases. 🛡️ Safe Area Support Automatically positions UI elements within the screen’s safe area (ideal for notched or rounded screens). 💾 Persistent Settings Built-in support for saving and loading UI scaler settings via PlayerPrefs, with a customizable interface for your own advanced save/load logic. 🧩 Scaler Grouping System Group UI scalers for better organization and apply settings across multiple canvases effortlessly. 🎚️ Player-Controlled UI Scaling Allow players to customize the scale of the UI to suit their preferences. 📏 Flexible Expansion Control Easily manage how your UI expands from your reference resolution to the full screen (ideal for wide and ultra wide displays). 🛠️ Editor Tools Included Test UI layouts directly in the Editor, with safe area simulation and real-time scaling previews. Requirements ❗ Unity 2022.3.0 or newer

manual/custom_ui_scaler.html.title: Custom UI Scaler | Smart UI Scaler plugin
manual/custom_ui_scaler.html.keywords: Custom UI Scaler Custom UI Scaler needs to be created when parent Canvas has "Camera Screen Space" Render Mode and attached camera renders to Render Texture, as Smart UI Scaler component cant receive the screen space area of the rendered image of the Canvas. To create a Custom UI Scaler extend the CoreUIScaler. These two methods must be implemented: Provide the screen space Rect of the Render Textures output image. protected abstract Rect GetScreenRect() Convert screen space Rect to world space Rect. protected abstract Rect ScreenRectToWorldRect(Rect screenRect)

manual/getting_started.html.title: Getting started | Smart UI Scaler plugin
manual/getting_started.html.keywords: Getting started This guide will help you to setup the initial Smart UI Scaler. Create a new GameObject inside your Canvas; Add the Smart UI Scaler component to this GameObject. The Rect Transform of this GameObject will be driven by Smart UI Scaler and will automatically resize; At first the Smart UI Scaler will work in "Fitted Reference Resolution" mode. You can see in Scene View that Canvas is represented with gray border and Smart UI Scaler has green border. This mode is recommended for editing UI layouts inside Smart UI Scaler and to place objects without overlapping; Lets add some UI objects into our Smart UI Scaler. As an example here is 4 added Raw Images anchored to the corners of the Smart UI Scaler; Now to test the Smart UI Scaler component with our UI layout we can open "Smart UI Scaler" editor window under "Tools" > "Smart UI Scaler"; This tool helps to test scaling without entering into Play Mode. Here we can change the current scaling mode into "Preview". This mode works exactly as it would in Play Mode; We can now see that out Smart UI Scaler takes up full area of the Canvas. Now you can test all the Smart UI Scaler component options to see them in effect; Note In "Preview" mode Smart UI Scalers border changes into Red color. This indicates that it is not advised to change the inner UI layout in this mode. Change back the "Scaling Mode" in "Smart UI Scaler" editor window to "Fitted Reference Resolution". Smart UI Scaler component will resize to reference resolution and you can continue to work on your UI layout. At this point you can remove the Canvas Scaler component from the Canvas object as it is no longer needed. Note As an alternative, closing the "Smart UI Scaler" window will also rest the "Scaling Mode" to "Fitted Reference Resolution". These steps showcase the basics of creating and testing your UI layout with an initial setup.

manual/smart_ui_expander_component.html.title: Smart UI Expander component | Smart UI Scaler plugin
manual/smart_ui_expander_component.html.keywords: Smart UI Expander component Used to expand Rect Transform outside of the parent UI Scaler to match parent Canvas borders. How it works Smart UI Expander component depends on parent Rect Transform. It follows this parent Rect Transforms size and uses it as a base from where to expand to Canvas borders. The four expansion fields are used to tell the Smart UI Expander to what directions it should expand. Showcase Here is a simple example. The black rectangle represent the safe area, it goes up all the way to the top border of the screen. The header is at the top and its background with teal color has the Smart UI Expander component. In the first image you can see that the header is inside the safe area and the Smart UI Expander does not do anything as no expansion field is selected. After we set the expansion to left and right borders of the screen we can now see that the header expands outside the safe area to full length of the screen. You can find the implementation of this example inside the Demo 3 of the plugin.

manual/smart_ui_scaler_component.html.title: Smart UI Scaler component | Smart UI Scaler plugin
manual/smart_ui_scaler_component.html.keywords: Smart UI Scaler component The main component of this plugin that replaces the built-in Canvas Scaler component. Group field Used to assign this Smart UI Scaler into a shared group with shared options. For more information see UI Scaler groups. Options fields These options are used when this Smart UI Scaler is not assigned into a group. Field Description Reference Resolution The baseline resolution that your UI layout was designed for. Use Safe Area Make use of only the screens safe area or the whole screen area. Alignment Controls the alignment inside Canvas screen area. Content Scale Controls the children scale. Recommended scale is [0.1, 1.0]. Expand Progress Controls occupied space between reference resolution and Canvas screen area. Allowed value is [0.0, 1.0]. Warning This UI Scaler only works in Canvases with "Overlay Screen Space" Render Mode or "Camera Screen Space" Render Mode where attached camera is rendering directly to the screen. When attached camera renders to Render Texture - this UI Scaler cant receive the screen space area of the rendered image and this information should be additionally provided.

manual/smart_ui_scaler_editor_window.htm.title: Smart UI Scaler editor window | Smart UI Scaler plugin
manual/smart_ui_scaler_editor_window.htm.keywords: Smart UI Scaler editor window Smart UI Scaler window helps to test and debug UI layouts. It can be found under "Tools" > "Smart UI Scaler"; Presets field This field is used to apply preset values to Smart UI Scaler window using presets scriptable object. To create a new presets scriptable object Right Click on Project Window then navigate to "SmartUIScaler" > "Editor" > "UIScalerEditorPresets". Warning UIScalerEditorPresets scriptable object should be placed inside "Editor" folder as this scriptable object only works in Editor. Presets scriptable object has the same options as Smart UI Scaler window. Presets options will be applied when Presets scriptable object is selected. They can be reapplied by pressing the "Reapply Presets" button. Scaling Mode field Scaling Mode field controls how UI Scalers are scaled in Edit Mode. Scaling Mode Description Fitted Reference Resolution Sets the size of UI Scalers to reference resolution and scales them to fit inside their Canvases. This mode is recommended for UI development and is most convenient to work with. Reference Resolution Sets the size of UI Scalers to reference resolution and keeps the scale to represent their reference resolution 1:1 in Unity units. This mode is also intended for UI development. Preview Enables full UI Scalers resizing that represents how UI Scalers will look like in Play Mode. It is not recommended to edit the inner UI layout when this mode is enabled. Note This field only works in Edit Mode and is ignored in Play Mode. Simulate Safe Area and Area fields These fields control the simulated screen safe area. To activate the safe area simulation enable the "Simulate Safe Area" toggle. The Area fields control the virtual displays borders padding around the safe area. Note Safe area simulation fields also work in Play Mode.

manual/smart_ui_size_limiter_component.h.title: Smart UI Size Limiter component | Smart UI Scaler plugin
manual/smart_ui_size_limiter_component.h.keywords: Smart UI Size Limiter component Limits the size of the Rect Transform to assigned min and max aspect ratios. Field Description Reference Height Height that is set to Rect Transform and used to calculate width for current aspect ratio. Cant be lower or equal to 0. Min Aspect Ratio Minimum limit for aspect ratio. For unlimited min aspect ratio - set the value to 0. Max Aspect Ratio Maximum limit for aspect ratio. For unlimited max aspect ratio - set the value to 0. How it works Smart UI Size Limiter component depends on parent Rect Transform. It uses the parents Rect Transform size to calculate the appropriate aspect ratio of Smart UI Size Limiter Rect Transform. If parents size is between the allowed min and max aspect ratios then the full parents size will be occupied, otherwise it will be limited. Note Smart UI Size Limiter component can work without UI Scaler in parent hierarchy.

manual/ui_scaler_groups.html.title: UI Scaler groups | Smart UI Scaler plugin
manual/ui_scaler_groups.html.keywords: UI Scaler groups UI Scaler Groups are used to share and control UI Scaler options between UI Scalers. UI Scaler Groups are controlled through their scriptable objects. To create a UI Scaler Group scriptable object Right Click on Project Window then navigate to "SmartUIScaler" > "UIScalerGroup". UI Scaler Group scriptable object has the "Default Options" dropdown fields that can be changed in the inspector. As the name suggests, these options are used initially. Once they are changed through UI Scaler Group scriptable object scripting API they will be overwritten. To assign a Smart UI Scaler to this group drag UI Scaler Group scriptable object into Smart UI Scaler "Group" field. Smart UI Scaler "Options" field will disappear as these options will no longer be used. UI Scaler Group options can be changed through scripting API using the UI Scaler Group scriptable object reference (UIScalerGroupSo API). Once the options are changed - all active UI Scalers will automatically update. Check out the Demo 2 inside the plugin, where a complete UI Scaler Group example is showcased. Initially UI Scaler Group options are not saved and loaded. To have persistent UI Scaler Group options the easiest way is to use UI Scaler Groups Persistence Manager component. Just add this component to an empty GameObject in the first scene in your project. It works by saving the options into PlayerPrefs when the game is closed and loads these options when this component awakes. For more advanced scenarios a custom saving and loading can be implemented through UIScalerGroups class GetSaveData() and SetSaveData(UIScalerGroupsSaveData) static methods.
